Once considered one of the finest ODI batsmen in the world, this Indian captain led three World Cup campaigns in the 1990s before a life ban for match-fixing ended his career — who is he?

Mohammad Azharuddin: Indian cricketer. Mohammad Azizuddin Azharuddin (born 8 February 1963) is an Indian politician and a former cricketer who also served as the Indian national cricket team's captain.
A United States war crime on 16 March 1968, this massacre in South Vietnam involved the mass murder of unarmed civilians, with some women and children gang-raped and mutilated. What tragedy is this?
My Lai massacre: 1968 U.S. war crime during the Vietnam War.
Widely seen as ill-prepared to rule a vast empire, he was the last monarch to reign before the Russian Revolution and led his country into World War I — which emperor?
Nicholas II: Emperor of Russia from 1894 to 1917.
Succeeding his kinsman as ruler of Novgorod, this Varangian prince extended control along the Dnieper to Kiev and led a successful raid on Constantinople before his death in 912 — who was he?
Oleg the Wise: Varangian prince, founder of Kievan Rus'

After the French Army's defeat by Germany in the Franco-Prussian War, radicalized National Guard soldiers seized control of the French capital on 18 March 1871, killed two army generals, and governed for about two months — what was this revolutionary government called?
This French politician founded the history-themed Puy du Fou theme park in Vendée and ran for president in 1995 and 2007 under the banner of the Movement for France — who is he?
Philippe de Villiers: French politician and essayist (born 1949)
Born from a 1525 secularization of a crusading order's lands and ruled for centuries by the House of Hohenzollern, this state forged the German Empire in 1871 — what was it?
Prussia: German state from 1525 to 1947. Prussia (German: Preußen [ˈpʁɔʏsn̩]; Old Prussian: Prūsija) was a German state centred on the North European Plain.
An Abrahamic faith born in 1930s Jamaica, it has no central authority and centers on Jah — with many followers regarding Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia as the Second Coming. What is it?
Rastafari: Abrahamic new religious movement originating in 1930s Jamaica.

This American fantasy author sold more than 90 million copies of his 14-book epic saga, having earlier in his career written tie-in novels featuring a sword-and-sorcery barbarian created by another writer. Who is he?
A Lemhi Shoshone teen who traveled thousands of miles from North Dakota to the Pacific with Lewis and Clark, she was later adopted as a suffrage-era symbol of women's worth — who was she?
This Germanic people had a semi-legendary hero named Widukind who fought against Charlemagne's Frankish forces — who were they?
Saxons: Medieval cultural group from what is now Northern Germany.
Centered on Marib and Sirwah in what's now Yemen, this ancient kingdom was considered the birthplace of South Arabian civilization and once expanded into the Horn of Africa. Which kingdom?
Sheba: Ancient South Arabian kingdom. Sheba, or Saba, was an ancient South Arabian kingdom that existed in Yemen before 275 CE.
An architect by training who once served as mayor of Quito, this man won Ecuador's presidency on his third try in 1992 after founding a new conservative party — who is it?
Sixto Durán Ballén: President of Ecuador from 1992 to 1996.
This Roman general became the first in the late Republic to march on Rome and win a civil war, later resigning his dictatorship after enacting constitutional reforms — who is he?
Sulla: Roman general and dictator (138–78 BC)
Also called the Decalogue, these covenant directives were given to Moses atop Mount Sinai and later smashed after he found the Israelites worshipping a golden calf. What are they?
Ten Commandments: Biblical principles relating to ethics and worship.
Born Joaquim José da Silva Xavier, this leader of Brazil's Inconfidência Mineira independence plot was hanged in 1792 and is now a national hero — by what one-word nickname is he remembered?
Tiradentes: 18th-century Brazilian revolutionary and national hero.

Formed after the Napoleonic Wars by fusing the old Dutch Republic, the Austrian-ruled Low Countries, and the Prince-Bishopric of Liège into a buffer state under William I of Orange-Nassau, this polity collapsed with the 1830 Belgian Revolution — what was it called?
United Kingdom of the Netherlands: European territory (1815–1839)

A protégé of murdered dissident Boris Nemtsov, this Russian-British activist and filmmaker has served as vice-chairman of an NGO founded by an exiled former oligarch, and received the Civil Courage Prize in 2018 after being repeatedly targeted for his opposition to the Kremlin. Who is he?
Who is this — “Female figure and also place of evil mentioned in the Book of Revelation”?
Whore of Babylon: Female figure and also place of evil mentioned in the Book of Revelation.

Founded by Modu Chanyu after overthrowing the Yuezhi, this nomadic tribal confederation dominated the eastern Eurasian steppe for centuries before a long conflict with the Han dynasty split it apart — what was this confederation called?
Xiongnu: Eurasian steppe confederation and empire. Modu Chanyu, the supreme leader after 209 BC, founded the Xiongnu Empire.

Once one of the nine members of China's most powerful decision-making body, this former security chief was arrested on corruption charges in 2014 after a career that began in the oil and gas industry — who is he?
Which of these people was born first?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Williamina Fleming is an astronomer. Williamina Paton Stevens Fleming (15 May 1857 – 21 May 1911) was a Scottish astronomer.
Who among these is a mathematician?
Carl Friedrich Gauss is a mathematician. Gauss was director of the Göttingen Observatory in Germany and professor of astronomy from 1807 until his death in 1855.
What is the atomic number of Rutherfordium?
Rutherfordium: Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
What is the atomic number of Selenium?
Selenium: Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
In what year was Buzz Aldrin born?
Buzz Aldrin: Buzz Aldrin ( AWL-drin; born Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr.; January 20, 1930) is an American former astronaut, aeronautical engineer, and fighter pilot.
In what year was Christine Lagarde born?
Christine Lagarde: Lagarde had also served in the Government of France, most prominently as Minister of the Economy, Finance and Industry from 2007 until 2011.
In what year was Ernest Rutherford born?
Ernest Rutherford: Together with Thomas Royds, Rutherford is credited with proving that alpha radiation is composed of helium nuclei.
In what year did Arthur Conan Doyle die?
Arthur Conan Doyle: Sir Arthur Ignatius Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 – 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
In what year did Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz die?
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz: Leibniz, along with René Descartes and Baruch Spinoza, was one of the three influential early modern rationalists.
In what year was Oxygen discovered?
Oxygen: Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
Potassium chloride: Pfizer. Potassium chloride (KCl, or potassium salt) is a metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine.
Rendang: Indonesia. It refers to both a cooking method of frying and the dish cooked in that way.
Who is credited with discovering Musca?
Musca: Petrus Plancius. Musca (Latin for 'the fly') is a small constellation in the deep southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Testosterone?
Testosterone: János Freud. Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males.
Who is credited with discovering Cyanoacrylate?
Cyanoacrylate: Harry Coover. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
Who is credited with discovering Rubidium?
Rubidium: Robert Bunsen. Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
This Swiss chemist discovered the structure of chitin in 1929 and decades later authored a memoir titled 'LSD: My Problem Child' — who was he?
Albert Hofmann (11 January 1906 - 29 April 2008) was a Swiss chemist known for being the first to synthesize, ingest, and learn of the psychedelic effects of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD).
Whether from too few red blood cells or faulty hemoglobin, this disorder leaves the blood less able to carry oxygen — often felt as quiet tiredness long before any paleness shows — what is it?
Anemia (also spelt anaemia in British English) is a blood disorder in which the blood has a reduced ability to carry oxygen.
With a tough, leathery shell and long claws for digging, this placental mammal native to the Americas has 21 living species and close relatives among anteaters and sloths — what animal is it?
Armadillo (Spanish for 'little armored ones') are placental mammals in the order Cingulata.

Developed in Great Britain around the 1830s from breeds like the Talbot Hound, this scent hound — smaller than the similar-looking foxhound — was originally bred to hunt rabbits and hares — name the breed?
Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
Native to cool parts of Europe and Asia, this deciduous shrub produces small, glossy black berries especially rich in vitamin C and vulnerable to cold snaps during spring flowering — name the fruit?
Blackcurrant (Ribes nigrum), black currant or cassis is a deciduous shrub in the family Grossulariaceae grown for its edible berries.

Forced to flee Italy in 1938 under the racial laws, this experimental physicist had earlier invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to show cosmic rays arrived more strongly from the West than the East — who was he?
Bruno Rossi (13 April 1905 - 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.
A child prodigy who became director of the Göttingen Observatory, this German polymath left his mark on number theory, algebra, geometry, statistics, and probability alike — who is he?
Carl Friedrich Gauss (30 April 1777 - 23 February 1855) was a German mathematician, astronomer, geodesist, and physicist, who contributed to many fields in mathematics and science.
Atomic number 17, this strongly oxidising yellow-green gas sits between fluorine and bromine on the periodic table — what element is it?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
This bird group's rock-dove species gave rise to most domesticated pigeon breeds, including racing and fantail pigeons, and was later introduced to the Americas — which classification is it?
Columba (genus) comprises a genus of medium to large pigeons.
This actor known for eccentric roles broke out playing a teenager's awkward father in a 1985 time-travel classic. Who is he?
Crow is a bird of the genus Corvus, or more broadly, a synonym for all of Corvus.
Its genus name translates to 'two-crested lizard,' honoring the twin head-crests found on fossils unearthed in Arizona in the 1940s — which Early Jurassic predator is this?
Dilophosaurus (dy-, -foh-) is a genus of theropod dinosaurs that lived in what is now North America during the Early Jurassic, about 186 million years ago.
Element 99 was first found in the radioactive debris of the very first hydrogen bomb blast in 1952 — which synthetic actinide is it?
Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Es and atomic number 99 and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element.
Also called grain alcohol, this volatile compound with the formula C2H5OH is the active ingredient in every alcoholic beverage — what is it?
Ethanol (also called ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol, or simply alcohol) is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH3CH2OH.
Found on sperm cells, fungal spores and countless microbes, this tail-like structure provides motility and even senses moisture in some swarming bacteria — what is it?

Flagellum (pl.: flagella) (Latin for 'whip' or 'scourge') is a hair-like appendage that protrudes from certain plant and animal sperm cells, from fungal spores (zoospores), and from a wide range of microorganisms to provide motility.
Native to Pacific coastal waters from Alaska to Baja California, this giant burrowing clam can grow a siphon over three feet long and live for more than a century — which creature?
Geoduck (Panopea generosa) is a species of very large saltwater clam in the family Hiatellidae.
One of only two wild camelid species native to South America, this llama relative lives at lower elevations than its cousin, the vicuña — what is it called?
Guanaco (gwah-; Lama guanicoe) is a camelid native to South America, closely related to the domesticated llama.

Named from the Greek for 'different wings' because most species have forewings that are part membrane, part hardened shell, this group of 40,000 insect species is the one most consistently called 'true bugs' — name this insect group?
Heteroptera are a group of about 40,000 species of insects in the order Hemiptera.
This birth defect, found in roughly one in every 250 newborn boys, involves an opening that fails to form in its typical location — what condition is this?

Hypospadias is a common malformation in fetal development, most commonly noticed in penises, in which the urethra does not open from its usual location on the head of the penis, or the middle of the vulva.
This Mexican neurophysiologist studied shamanism, meditation, and telepathy through the scientific method, writing more than 50 books before vanishing in December 1994 — who is he?
Jacobo Grinberg (born Mexico City in 1946) was a Mexican neurophysiologist and psychologist.
This Mexican-American astronaut flew on STS-128, led a branch at Johnson Space Center, and — urged on by President Obama — ran for Congress in 2012; who is he?
José M. Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
He stepped down as CEO of Google in 2001 only to return a decade later, then led its new parent Alphabet; which co-founder is now among the world's wealthiest people?
Larry Page (born March 26, 1973) is an American businessman and computer scientist who co-founded Google with Sergey Brin.
Equal to one cubic decimetre, this metric unit of volume was originally a base unit of the French metric system and derives its name from an old French unit of weight. What unit is it?

Litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used:) is a metric unit of volume. It is equal to 1 cubic decimetre (dm3), 1000 cubic centimetres (cm3) or 0.001 cubic metres (m3).
With about 6,640 living species across 27 orders — rodents and bats leading the count — this class of vertebrates feeds its young on milk. What is it?
Mammal (from Latin mamma 'breast') is a vertebrate animal of the class Mammalia.
Nicknamed "quicksilver," this is the only metallic element that stays liquid at room temperature, and it's often mined as the red mineral cinnabar — which element is it?
Mercury (element) is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
In 1812 Étienne Geoffroy grouped the apes with the Cercopithecidae under the name Catarrhini, or "Old World" members of this familiar simian group — what common name is it?
Monkey is a common name that may refer to most mammals of the infraorder Simiiformes, also known as simians.
This silvery lanthanide, found in the minerals monazite and bastnäsite, is about as common as cobalt or nickel despite its 'rare earth' label — which element?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Many species in this bird family scavenge alongside pigeons and gulls, while two of its city-dwelling members are famous for nesting directly on buildings — which family are they?
Old World sparrow are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
Members of the family Phasianidae and native to Eurasia, these game birds snack on insects and fresh green shoots come summer — what are they?
Pheasant are birds of several genera within the family Phasianidae in the order Galliformes.
Built from poetic devices like onomatopoeia, rhyme schemes, and rhythm, this literary art uses the musical qualities of language to suggest more than the words plainly say — what is it?

Poetry (from the Greek word poiesis, "making") is a form of literary art that uses aesthetic and often rhythmic qualities of language to evoke meanings in addition to, or in place of, literal or surface-level meanings.
Belonging to the rose family, this flowering tree species gives us most plums, including the greengage and damson varieties — which species is it?
Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.

Rooted in Minangkabau cooking, this dish slow-simmers meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — both a method and a meal across the Malacca Strait; what is it?

Rendang is a fried meat or dry curry made of meat stewed in coconut milk and spices, widely popular across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the southern parts of the Philippines, where each version is considered local cuisine.
A botanist active in Japan's Meiji era, this scholar died in 1899 after decades of scientific work — who was he?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (October 13, 1851 - August 8, 1899) was a Japanese botanist during the Meiji era.
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Born in the Bronx to Puerto Rican parents and raised by her mother after her father's death, this Princeton grad became the third woman on the U.S. Supreme Court after Barack Obama's 2009 appointment — name this justice?
Sonia Sotomayor (born June 25, 1954) is an American lawyer and jurist who serves as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
In the equation 5 − 2 = 3, this is the operation being performed — which one is it?
Subtraction (which is signified by the minus sign) is one of the four arithmetic operations along with addition, multiplication and division.
Caused by Clostridium tetani, this infection brings on recurring muscle spasms that can last weeks and prove fatal in about 10% of cases — what is it commonly known as?
Tetanus (from Ancient Greek 'tension', 'stretched', 'rigid'), also known as lockjaw, is a bacterial infection caused by Clostridium tetani and characterized by muscle spasms.
Roughly eight times more potent than an older analogue, this bleeding-control medication is also prescribed for hereditary angioedema — what is it?
Tranexamic acid is a medication used to treat or prevent excessive blood loss from major trauma, postpartum bleeding, surgery, tooth removal, nosebleeds, and heavy menstruation.
Just 25 light-years away, this is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and the fifth-brightest star in the entire night sky — what is it?
Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
Inspired by the code-breaking game Mastermind, this once-a-day puzzle gives you six tries and colored tiles to crack the same word everyone else is solving — which game?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Wordle is a web-based word game created and developed by the Welsh software engineer Josh Wardle.
The simplest and smallest ketone, this colorless, pungent, highly flammable liquid mixes freely with water and lurks in nail polish remover and paint thinner — what is it?
Working at Baghdad's House of Wisdom around 820, this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote a treatise whose Arabic title, Al-Jabr, gave us the very word "algebra." Who was he?
Sometimes called 'pigweed,' this genus of plants is grown worldwide as a leaf vegetable and for its edible grain — which genus?
Amaranth: Genus of plants. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a succulent, hollow stem.
Native to the eastern Mediterranean, this flowering herb's seeds taste similar to fennel, licorice, and tarragon and flavor candies and spirits — what is it?
Native to the northern tundra, this small mammal grows thick white fur for winter camouflage and forms monogamous breeding pairs while preying on lemmings and seabirds — what animal is it?
Arctic fox: Species of fox. It is well adapted to living in cold environments, and is known for its thick, warm fur that can be used as camouflage against snow in the winter.

This rapid, irregular quivering of the heart's upper chambers can be entirely silent or bring palpitations and fainting — and it sharply raises the risk of stroke, dementia and heart failure. What is this arrhythmia?
Atrial fibrillation: Irregular beating of the atria of the heart.
Belonging to genus Fagus, this deciduous tree yields timber used for furniture, flooring, and plywood, and its wood also makes excellent firewood. What is this tree?
Beech: Genus of trees in the family Fagaceae.

After serving as creative director at Xanga in the early 2000s, this entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, then later launched a visual-search engine called Jelly that was acquired by Pinterest in 2017. Who is he?
Biz Stone: American blogger and co-founder of Twitter (born 1974)
Named in honor of physicist Satyendra Nath Bose and coined by Paul Dirac, this class of subatomic particle has integer spin and includes force carriers like gluons and the Higgs — what is it called?
Boson: Class of subatomic particle. In particle physics, a boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
Belonging to the superfamily Papilionoidea, these brightly winged insects pass through a chrysalis stage, and their oldest fossils date to about 56 million years ago — what are they?
Butterfly: Group of insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.

Medieval German miners cursed an ore that looked metal-rich but smelted into nothing useful, naming it after a mischievous goblin — yet for centuries its blue pigment tinted glass and jewelry. Which element, symbol Co, atomic number 27, earned that goblin's name?
Cobalt: Chemical element with atomic number 27 (Co)
Considered the most renowned Greek mathematician since antiquity, he advanced measure theory and the calculus of variations and even gave thermodynamics an axiomatic formulation — who is it?
Native to the Andes and Mesoamerica, this plant genus includes five edible species known variously as squash, pumpkin or gourd — which genus?
Native to Madagascar and grown ornamentally throughout the tropics, this legume tree is known for its fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red blossoms — what is it?
Delonix regia: Species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.
One of the Hungarian émigré scientists nicknamed the "Martians," he extended Fermi's theory of beta decay and is colloquially called the father of the hydrogen bomb — who was he?

Dubbed a 'living fossil' and commonly known as horsetail, this spore-reproducing plant genus once included 30-meter-tall trees in Carboniferous forests, its node-spacing pattern said to have inspired the invention of logarithms — which genus?

With a rich chestnut crown and a bold black patch on each white cheek, this small Old World songbird nests in cavities, walls, or abandoned magpie nests, and lays five or six eggs that hatch in under two weeks — which bird?
Eurasian tree sparrow: Species of bird. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult.
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
This Italian-American economist taught at MIT's Sloan School and Carnegie Mellon before collecting the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics. Who was he?
Franco Modigliani: Italian-American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2003)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Dubbed the 'king of the birds' in European folklore for its golden head crest, this tiny kinglet's scientific name literally means 'petty king' — which bird?
Goldcrest: Small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.

Often triggered by a preceding throat infection, this childhood autoimmune disease causes raised skin bruising, joint pain, and sometimes kidney trouble from IgA immune-complex deposits — what is it called?
Henoch–Schönlein purpura: Autoimmune vascular inflammatory disease.
Defined today as exactly 3,600 seconds, this unit of time was originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East — which unit?
Hour: Unit of time equal to 60 minutes.
Native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the Caspian region, this mint-family shrub has long been used in traditional herbal medicine as an antiseptic and cough reliever — which plant?

Hyssopus officinalis: Species of plant. Hyssopus officinalis or hyssop is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
An English polymath who was also an alchemist and theologian, he shares credit with Leibniz for inventing calculus and wrote the Principia — who is he?
Part of a four-person extremist cell known for English accents, this Kuwaiti-born militant appeared in Islamic State videos before being killed in a 2015 drone strike near Raqqa — who is he?
Jihadi John: Kuwaiti-British terrorist and ISIS executioner (1988–2015)
Named for a district in Turkey's Sivas Province, which large livestock guardian breed has been exported to Africa to protect flocks from cheetahs?
Kangal Shepherd Dog: Turkish breed of dog. The Kangal Shepherd Dog or Turkish Kangal (Turkish: Kangal Çoban Köpeği) is a traditional Turkish breed of large livestock guardian dog.
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
As a principal shareholder of L'Oréal, this French heiress was the richest woman in the world at the time of her death in 2017, worth $44.3 billion — who was she?
Liliane Bettencourt: French heiress, socialite and businesswoman (1922–2017)
Native to Africa except for one species found only on Madagascar, this small parrot gets its common name from its strong, monogamous pair-bonding behavior — what is it?
Oblate rather than round, with a thin, loose peel that makes it easy to separate into segments, this citrus fruit is sweeter and stronger-tasting than its spherical, hybrid cousin — which fruit?
Mandarin orange: Small citrus fruit. A mandarin orange (Citrus reticulata), often simply called mandarin, is a small, rounded citrus tree fruit.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
This scientific field studies microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and protists, encompassing sub-disciplines like virology and mycology — which discipline?

Thought to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' and a reduced risk of inbreeding-linked health problems, this catch-all term covers roughly 150 million dogs worldwide that don't belong to any officially recognized breed — what's it called?
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
This synthetic element 113 was claimed by both a Russian-American team at Dubna and, in 2004, a Japanese team at Riken. What's its name?
Nihonium: Chemical element with atomic number 113 (Nh)
Native to East Africa and known in some places as 'lady's fingers,' this mallow-family plant is prized for its edible green (sometimes red) seed pods — what is it?

Produced in the hypothalamus and nicknamed for its role in love and social bonding, this peptide hormone also doubles as a pharmaceutical that speeds up childbirth by triggering uterine contractions — what is it?
Oxytocin: Peptide hormone and neuropeptide. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
The males of this pheasant-family bird are famed for piercing calls and extravagant plumage; its Asiatic, green, and Congo species span India to central Africa — what common name covers them all?
Peafowl: Group of large game birds.
This inherited metabolic disorder, caused by mutations in the PAH gene, leaves patients unable to break down a certain amino acid and can give off a musty odor if untreated — what is it?
Phenylketonuria: Amino acid metabolic disorder. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
First classified as its own fossil order in 1835, this group of Mesozoic marine reptiles thrived through the Jurassic before dying out at the end of the Cretaceous — what are they called?
Plesiosaur: Order of reptiles (fossil). The Plesiosauria or plesiosaurs are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
This New World family within the order Carnivora encompasses raccoons, ringtails, coatis, and kinkajous, most of them omnivorous — what family is it?
Procyonidae: Family of mammals. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Native to southern China, this pear tree's fruit goes by dozens of names worldwide - Asian pear, apple pear, nashi pear - but is rarely baked into pies due to its high water content - which species?
Pyrus pyrifolia: Species of pear with round crisp grainy fruit.
Scholars call it an "essentially contested concept" with no agreed definition, but it broadly links humanity to the supernatural through behaviors, ethics, texts and sacred places — what is it?
This enormous flowering-plant family, named for its type genus, gives us apples, cherries, strawberries, and ornamental roses alike — which plant family is it?
Rosaceae: Rose family of flowering plants.
